findings.description: The round-parked event still carries only `patchable`, so the one line `scrat watch` and `scrat logs` print for a parked round is `roundParkedSentence` = "round %d is waiting on you: %d findings can be patched" (internal/presentation/messages.go:38, rendered at internal/presentation/presentation.go:47). Before this change a round could only park on blocking auto-fix findings, so that count was always >= 1 and fully described what the round waited on. Now a round parks on questions too, and the count is silently wrong. Concrete path: the scenario already in the suite at internal/e2e/readonly_test.go:77 returns exactly one finding, `{"severity":"warning","action":"ask-user"}`. Under the new rule that run parks (the test was changed to wait for `awaiting-response`). `classified.Patchable` is empty, so `scrat watch` on that run prints "round 1 is waiting on you: 0 findings can be patched" and nothing else about what it waits on. README.md:57 was updated to promise that watch stops for a round parked "on a question somebody has to answer", but the line it then prints reports zero. `scrat status` gained a count for this (report.Status.AwaitingAPerson); the park event did not.

The rewritten escalated branch states "A run escalates for one of two reasons, and scrat status prints which: a finding holds the change while its own action asks for nothing ... or the last permitted round still found something blocking." `scrat status` prints a positive marker for only one of the two. `verdictReason` (internal/reviewer/supervise.go:253) appends `theCapWasReached` when `dialogue.EscalatedByTheCap`, and otherwise emits `whatAReviewerFound` = "a reviewer reported %d findings, %d of them for the person, ..." with `len(classified.NeedingAPerson)` - a count of `ask-user` findings, which after this change never cause an escalation. Trace a round returning one `{"severity":"error","action":"no-op"}` finding: the run escalates, exit 1, and status prints `verdict: a reviewer reported 1 findings, 0 of them for the person, ...` plus `findings: 1 in total, 0 for the person, 0 to patch, 1 informational`. The finding that caused the escalation is labelled "informational" (report.Audience maps NoOp to `informationalAudience`) and nothing names the reason, so the session is told to hand everything to the person while every count says nothing is for them. Before the change the non-cap escalation reason was an `ask-user` finding, which the person-count did report positively, so the sentence held; it does not now.

Switching these two seal tests from `WaitForTerminal` to `WaitFor(name, runstate.AwaitingResponse)` made their named assertions unreachable. `reason(run)` (internal/e2e/shared_test.go:29) returns the literal "no verdict" when `run.Verdict == nil`, and `Supervision.park` never sets a verdict, so `strings.Contains(reason(run), "wrote to the snapshot worktree")` here and `strings.Contains(reason(run), ".serena")` at line 111 can no longer be true for any input - a regression that wrongly blamed the reviewer would end the run `failed` and be caught by `WaitFor`'s Fatalf instead, never by the assertion whose message states what the test is for. The stated behaviour ("a reviewer that wrote nothing was reported as having written", "a write the seal refused was reported against the reviewer") is now checked only incidentally. Replace the dead checks with ones that can fail against a parked run, e.g. assert the run carries no verdict and that no recorded event names the write.

The escalating scenario was rewritten to escalate via a blocking `no-op` finding, and a second finding `{"severity":"info"}` with no `action` was added alongside it. That second finding is what now satisfies `stdout 'needs a person'` under the comment "A review that finds something blocking exits one": it is non-blocking, it is not why the run escalated, and the finding that is why renders as "informational". The same padding keeps `stdout 'for the person'` alive at internal/e2e/testdata/script/reading.txtar:47, where the substring would match even for a count of zero. Both assertions still pass but no longer connect to escalation, so neither would notice the escalated surface losing its account of why it escalated.

risk_rationale: The routing rule itself is small, exhaustively tested over its whole input space, and the ordering fix in `Unanswered` is genuinely pinned by that test; what is unfinished is the reporting around the two states the rule moved, plus two assertions that stopped being able to fail.
